The hub's unlabeled version of it is under the notes (Telling the stages apart), and six picture questions use it. To name a stage: flat or cube-shaped cells? one layer or many? fluid in several spaces, or one big antrum? Theca interna: richly vascularized connective tissue. Its cells have LH receptors, and in response to LH they make androgens that are precursors to estrogen. Primordial One layer, squamous, joined by desmosomes Oocyte about 25 micrometers; no zona pellucida Early primary (unilaminar) One layer, cuboidal granulosa cells Zona pellucida starting to form; gap junctions Late primary (multilaminar) Several layers of granulosa cells Full zona; theca interna and externa organizing Secondary (antral) Many layers, with fluid among them Liquor folliculi and antrum; cumulus oophorus; corona radiata Graafian Granulosa cells around a large antrum About 20 millimeters; bulges on the ovary; prominent theca 2 Exam 2 in-class review (11/11): the corona radiata and the peg cells of the uterine tube; their twins, and the granulosa cells' gap junctions Exam 2 review · 5 questions in the bank Know this Know the tube's two cell types (ciliated cells beating toward the uterus, peg cells feeding the ovum), its folds in every region and its poorly defined muscularis. The granulosa cells develop extensive gap junctions with each other but no tight junctions, so there is no blood-follicle barrier. Compare the testis, where tight junctions between Sertoli cells form the blood-testis barrier. Its mucosa has longitudinal folds in all regions. The epithelium is simple columnar with two cell types: ciliated cells, whose wave of cilia is directed toward the uterus, and non-ciliated peg cells, which secrete a fluid that provides nutrients to the ovum. The muscularis is a poorly defined inner circular and outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle, not built for strong peristalsis, and the outer serosa is a simple squamous membrane. 3 Granulosa versus theca: junctions, the zona pellucida, liquor folliculi, LH and FSH Focus list + recording · 4 questions in the bank Granulosa cells proliferate into several layers, so the follicle is now multilaminar, and cortical granules start to develop at the outer edge of the oocyte. The zona pellucida surrounds the oocyte; it is produced by the follicular cells, and it is made of glycoproteins. His slide names them ZP1, ZP2 and ZP3, and he says you don't need to know those. Microvilli from the oocyte and filopodia from the granulosa cells penetrate the zona and touch each other, so the cells stay in contact across it. 4 FSH grows 10 to 12 antral follicles, LH matures and ovulates the dominant one; primordial to Graafian takes many months Focus list + recording · 3 questions in the bank Know this FSH grows the 10 to 12 antral follicles; LH, in the FSH plus LH surge, matures and ovulates the dominant one. FSH and LH split the work, and he went back a few slides to show it again: an FSH surge induces the growth of 10 to 12 antral follicles, one of which becomes dominant, with a huge antrum; it takes LH, in the FSH plus LH surge, to trigger maturation and ovulation of that dominant follicle. Dr. Madison covers the hypothalamic-pituitary axis behind it. 5 Uterine tube: ciliated and peg cells, folds in all regions, poorly defined muscularis, capacitation Focus list + recording · 5 questions in the bank His slide flags two points about the tube. First, the mucosa provides nutrients and protection for the oocyte and the sperm, and it produces factors that promote sperm activation, a process called capacitation. In the male lecture the epididymis holds capacitation back, so it happens only in the female tract. Second, the oocyte remains viable for only about 24 hours if it is not fertilized. 6 The uterine wall: endometrium (simple columnar epithelium, simple branched glands, functionalis with helical arteries and basalis), myometrium (inner longitudinal, middle circular with the stratum vasculare, outer longitudinal), perimetrium Focus list + recording · 3 questions in the bank Myometrium: most of the uterus. Inner longitudinal, middle circular and outer longitudinal smooth muscle. The middle circular layer carries numerous large blood vessels and is called the stratum vasculare. 7 The endometrium during menstruation: the functionalis (spiral arteries, follows estrogen and progesterone, shed) vs the basalis (straight arteries, untouched, regrows it); progesterone drops, the spiral arteries constrict, ischemia, shedding Focus list + recording · 4 questions in the bank Know this Menstruation: progesterone falls, the spiral arteries constrict, the functionalis goes hypoxic and sheds. Spiral arteries feed the functionalis; straight arteries feed the basalis, which is why it survives and regrows the lining. Marked with three asterisks on his slide, and explained twice in the recording: the drop in progesterone causes constriction of the spiral arteries, leading to local ischemia in the functional layer and its separation from the basal layer. Follow the chain. No pregnancy, so the corpus luteum degenerates. Progesterone falls. The spiral arteries of the functionalis contract periodically and cut off its oxygen, so the functionalis becomes hypoxic. The hypoxia breaks down the spiral arteries, which flood the lamina propria with blood, and the functionalis, its glands and decidua-like cells, detaches and is shed into the uterine cavity: menses, days 1 to 5. The basalis is not really affected, because its straight arteries give it an independent blood supply, and it regrows a new functionalis in the proliferative phase. 8 The two meiotic arrests: prophase I until the LH surge, metaphase II until fertilization Flagged in the recording · 3 questions in the bank Know this Two arrests, two releases: prophase I until the LH surge, metaphase II until fertilization (his three-asterisk slide). Marked with three asterisks on his slide, and said in the recording: all follicles within the ovary contain a primary oocyte arrested in prophase I. The LH surge causes the primary oocyte to complete meiosis I shortly before ovulation, producing a secondary oocyte. The secondary oocyte enters meiosis II and arrests at metaphase II until fertilization. Release two: fertilization. Only upon fertilization does the oocyte complete the second meiotic division, forming the ovum and a second polar body. Unfertilized, it stays viable about 24 hours. It causes the release of meiosis-inducing factor, which signals the primary oocyte to complete meiosis I, giving a secondary oocyte and one polar body. The secondary oocyte immediately enters meiosis II and stops at metaphase. 9 His cycle graph by day: follicles, ovulation on days 13 to 15, FSH and LH peaks, estrogen and progesterone, and the uterine phases Flagged in the recording · 4 questions in the bank Know this On his graph FSH peaks with LH just before ovulation (days 13 to 15). The hub follows his graph in every lecture; L16's slide says inhibin holds FSH down then. Estrogen: low, rising from about day 7 to a peak around day 12 or 13, a dip around days 15 to 17, a second, smaller rise around days 23 to 24, then down. His graph and his words give FSH a peak with LH at ovulation, a smaller peak than LH's, and the hub follows him in every lecture, the cycle figure included. L16's slide puts it differently (inhibin holding FSH down at midcycle); most physiology texts draw the small FSH peak beside the LH surge, as he does. 10 Ovulation: the LH surge, rupture into the peritoneum, and the corpus luteum's lutein cells and fate Flagged in the recording · 5 questions in the bank Granulosa cells of the Graafian follicle keep producing glycosaminoglycans and hyaluronic acid, which hold fluid, mostly water, so the antrum swells. The follicle enlarges, moves to the outer cortex and pushes against the capsule, the tunica albuginea, until the walls of both the ovary and the follicle rupture. The secondary oocyte and the cells of the corona radiata are released into the peritoneum, the abdominal cavity, near the opening of the oviduct, the infundibulum, which has to catch them and send them into the tube. The emptied follicle collapses and becomes folded, and LH converts it into the corpus luteum. Granulosa-lutein cells come from the granulosa cells of the Graafian follicle and make progesterone and estrogen. Theca-lutein cells come from the enlarged cells of the theca interna and make progesterone. 11 The linings of the cervix and vagina (the transformation zone, glycogen and lactobacilli) and the cervical plug Flagged in the recording · 3 questions in the bank Know this Cervix in pregnancy: a viscous mucus plug; and its abrupt switch to stratified squamous where it meets the vagina is the transformation zone. At ovulation, the cervical glands secrete a watery fluid that helps sperm migrate (on his slide). The part of the cervix that projects into the vagina is covered with stratified squamous epithelium. The abrupt change between the two linings is the transformation zone. Mucosa: stratified squamous epithelium over a highly vascular lamina propria with high numbers of lymphocytes and neutrophils. 12 Milk production (prolactin) versus ejection (oxytocin), and colostrum Flagged in the recording · 3 questions in the bank Know this Colostrum: the first 3 to 4 days, more protein and IgA; prolactin makes milk, oxytocin ejects it. Synthesis, or production Prolactin Secretion, or ejection (let-down) Oxytocin Colostrum is the milk produced for the first 3 to 4 days after birth. It has increased concentrations of proteins and immunoglobulin A, so a new mother's first milk is the most antibody-rich, not the weakest. 13 Oocyte numbers from the fetus to menopause Flagged in the recording · 2 questions in the bank Know this Know the falling numbers: 5 to 7 million by the 5th fetal month, 1 to 2 million at birth, about 400,000 at menarche, about 450 ovulated. 5th fetal month About 5 to 7 million primary oocytes; oogonia stop dividing Birth About 1 to 2 million, each in a follicle, arrested in prophase I Menarche About 400,000 Each month About 12 follicles start to grow; usually one ovulates Whole reproductive span About 450 ovulated 14 Pregnancy and the tract: corpus luteum kept, myometrium grows, cervical plug Core of the slides · 3 questions in the bank Together they make up the corpus luteum; its hormones make the progesterone peak on his graph. If pregnancy does not occur, the corpus luteum degenerates, and the old structure fills with fibroblasts that secrete collagen, becoming the white corpus albicans. If pregnancy does occur, the placenta produces a hormone that helps maintain the corpus luteum, and with it the progesterone that keeps the endometrium in place.
